label: Late-episode D1 ramp after a1->S1, gated by reward two trials back
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("reward", -3) == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0)**2
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only late in the episode (from about trial 70 on). Its size grows roughly with the square of (ep_trial - 70), but only when the previous trial was a1 reaching S1 (common). After a previous trial that reached S2 or used a2, it sits below the timing baseline. Within a1->S1 trials the reward history two trials back matters most: if trial -2 was unrewarded the activation is pushed to near zero, and a reward at trial -2 or -3 raises it. The previous trial reward on its own adds little. Activation is zero at GO and D2. The model value and policy deciles add nothing. All terms are observed-only, with no future or hidden variables. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.64 (dev 0.64). The profile additive all ceiling is only 0.17, because the shape is a multiplicative interaction of episode time and history. Shape is a quadratic ramp; an exponential ramp gave a slightly worse fit (dev 0.50 vs 0.51 in a 4-term version).

issues: Main claims reproduce. The original terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.6351. The model value and policy-logit terms add only 0.004 (0.639). GO and D2 copies of the ramp get weight 0.0. The previous trial's reward adds little: a1->S1 ramp alone scores 0.326, and adding prev_reward==0 brings it to 0.336, while adding tv('reward',-2)==0 brings it to 0.489.

Overclaim: 'drops to near zero'. The fitted net weight after an unrewarded trial -2 is about 0.0012 - 0.0017, but in the worst-fit windows the actual value falls from about 1.9-2.1 to about 0.65-0.71 (e.g. t98 after t97 r0: actual 0.71, predicted -0.06). So the drop is large but not to zero, and the model under-predicts these cases.

The cue at trial -2 is broader than its reward. Adding A*(state_-2 == S2) gets weight -0.00155, and A*(reward_-2 == 0 & state_-2 == S1) gets -0.0015, while the plain reward_-2 == 0 weight shrinks to -0.00016 (test 0.638). The activation drops whenever trial -2 was not S1-rewarded, not only when it was unrewarded. This is a description issue only; the R^2 change is small.

The 'reward at -2 or -3 raises it' terms mostly encode whether trial -2/-3 lies inside the window. Their weights (+0.00036, +0.00039) are small next to the base 0.0012. Together they lift R^2 from 0.49 to 0.51. Most of the gain to 0.635 comes from the below-baseline terms after a2 or S2.

The largest remaining misses are on the window's first trial, where prev_action and tv are unknown (actual about 2.0, predicted 0.32 from timing only), and on the size of the dip. This is a window-truncation artifact, not a missed behavioural class. The phase x previous-trial mean errors are all small (the largest is D1 after a1 S1 u at -0.028).
Adding an a2->S1 term and a window-start term only reaches 0.642. No large systematic gap remains.
